glossary.ipsilateral: On the same side of the body.
glossary.visual loss: Reduction or loss of sight in one or both eyes.
glossary.blurred vision: Loss of sharpness, so details look fuzzy.
glossary.colour vision: The ability to tell colours apart, carried mostly by cone cells and the optic nerve.
glossary.visual acuity: Sharpness of vision, measured with a letter chart.
glossary.visual field defect: An area of the field of vision where sight is missing or reduced.
glossary.dilated: Wider than normal; for a pupil, larger.
glossary.disc swelling: A raised, blurred optic disc seen on fundoscopy.
glossary.optic disc: The spot at the back of the eye where the optic nerve leaves, seen on fundoscopy.
glossary.glioma: A tumour arising from the brain's support cells; an optic nerve glioma can compress the nerve.
glossary.metastasis: A cancer deposit that has spread from its original site.
glossary.folate: A B vitamin needed for DNA synthesis; deficiency causes anaemia and can harm the optic nerve.
glossary.malignant hypertension: Very high blood pressure causing acute organ damage, including optic disc swelling.
glossary.sarcoidosis: A disease of non-caseating granulomas in many organs, including the eye and optic nerve.
glossary.TB: Tuberculosis, a bacterial infection usually of the lungs.
glossary.bladder dysfunction: Problems controlling or emptying the bladder, from spinal cord damage in NMO.
glossary.leg weakness: Reduced power in the legs, here from spinal cord inflammation.
glossary.neurology: The medical specialty for disorders of the brain, spinal cord and nerves.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging: a scan using magnets that shows soft tissue, including MS plaques.
glossary.contrast: A dye (gadolinium for MRI) that highlights active inflammation on scans.
glossary.demyelinating plaques: Areas where myelin has been stripped from nerves, seen as bright spots on MRI in MS.
glossary.IM: Intramuscular: given by injection into a muscle.
glossary.corticosteroids: Steroid drugs that reduce inflammation, such as prednisolone and methylprednisolone.
glossary.visual field testing: Mapping how much a person can see around them to find blind areas.
glossary.mimics: Other conditions that look similar and must be ruled out.
glossary.stroke: Sudden brain damage from a blocked or burst blood vessel.
glossary.visual pathway: The route from retina through optic nerve, chiasm and tracts to the visual cortex.
glossary.tapered: A dose reduced gradually rather than stopped suddenly.
glossary.ophthalmology: The medical specialty for eye disease.
glossary.conduction: Travel of electrical signals along a nerve fibre.
glossary.myelin: The fatty insulating sheath around nerve fibres that speeds conduction.
glossary.orbital fascia: Connective tissue sheets in the eye socket linking muscles and the optic nerve.
glossary.nerve sheath: The layers of tissue (meninges) wrapping the optic nerve.
glossary.afferent: Carrying signals towards the brain; the optic nerve is the afferent limb of the pupil reflex.
glossary.pupillary constriction: Narrowing of the pupil in response to light.
glossary.antibodies: Immune proteins that bind specific targets; in NMO they attack aquaporin-4.
glossary.oedema: Swelling from fluid in the tissues.
glossary.MS conversion: Going on to develop full multiple sclerosis after a first episode such as optic neuritis.
